name: Teresa Hsu
method: Muse Spark web search (2 calls) for leads; every fact below re-read from the cited page by the agent. corroborated = two or more independent sources.

facts.text: Born, by the usual account on 7 July 1898, in Kak Chioh, a village of Swatow (Shantou), Guangdong, in the last years of the Qing dynasty. Wikipedia notes the date was never independently verified.

sources.label: Heart to Heart Service, 'About Founder' and Sharana Rao's announcement (Wayback, 2012)
Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih
NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)

facts.text: She was the second of four children: an elder sister Ursula, a younger sister Lucy and a brother Anthony.

sources.label: Singapore Women's Hall of Fame (SCWO), 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (inducted 2014)
Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)

facts.text: At five or six she heard beggars telling their stories in the street outside; too small to see out of the window, she wanted to know why people suffered.
facts.quote: I may have been a girl of five or six when I heard beggars telling their sad tales along the street.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Khng Eu Meng, 'Teresa Hsu: Never too old to care for others', Singapore's Extraordinary People (1995), reprinted on cme4all wiki
The Straits Times, Friday Interview and timeline (31 Dec 1999), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: The family was so poor that at times she ate grass; she called picking grass to eat, 'very, very hungry', the hardest part of her life.
facts.quote: It was at that moment I thought to myself that no one should ever go through what I went through.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: K. Kasturi Dewi, 'The Power of Laughter', The Star (26 Jan 2010), reprinted on tsemrinpoche.com
NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)

facts.text: The children rose at 4 am to fill bamboo baskets with pine needles for fuel in the Swatow hills, then carried the same baskets of laundry to wash in the streams.
facts.quote: We rose at 4am to fill our bamboo baskets with pine needles as fuel.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)

facts.text: Her father was physically abusive and left the family for another woman; her illiterate mother raised the four children alone.

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih
Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)

facts.text: Her mother once dug up potatoes for the family's dinner and gave the whole pot to a starving beggar with a child at the door.
facts.quote: That was the day I learnt that to give what you have in your hand to others is a great blessing.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: K. Kasturi Dewi, 'The Power of Laughter', The Star (26 Jan 2010), reprinted on tsemrinpoche.com
SeniorsAloud, 'Meet Angel of Compassion - Teresa Hsu' (Dec 2008; author met her 20 Oct 2008)

facts.text: When the last uncle who supported them left, the family sold their lace for a boat passage to Penang; her grandmother, mother and three siblings went with her.

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)

facts.text: In Penang she and her mother worked as cleaners at a Catholic convent.

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
Singapore Women's Hall of Fame (SCWO), 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (inducted 2014)

facts.text: At 27, still unschooled, she persuaded the convent nuns to let her sit in on the children's classes; about three and a half years later she passed the Senior Cambridge examination.
facts.quote: The nuns got us free books from rich former pupils.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih
K. Kasturi Dewi, 'The Power of Laughter', The Star (26 Jan 2010), reprinted on tsemrinpoche.com

facts.text: The Star reports she ran away at 16 to escape an arranged marriage. The age and destination conflict with other accounts (see conflicts).

sources.label: K. Kasturi Dewi, 'The Power of Laughter', The Star (26 Jan 2010), reprinted on tsemrinpoche.com

facts.text: She left Penang for Hong Kong, cleaning by day and learning English, shorthand and typing by night, until she was hired as a stenographer.

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
The Straits Times, Friday Interview and timeline (31 Dec 1999), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: She moved to Chongqing as secretary and bookkeeper at a German news agency, then gave up the well-paid job to volunteer with the Friends' Ambulance Unit, a service run by English pacifists.

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih

facts.text: Facing the dying at the front, she decided her vocation was to nurse the sick and destitute.
facts.quote: The poor can at least beg, but the others, you either go to them, or they die.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
Khng Eu Meng, 'Teresa Hsu: Never too old to care for others', Singapore's Extraordinary People (1995), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: In the ambulance service she met Brian Sorenson, a 24-year-old blond, blue-eyed volunteer: the only time, she said, she came close to having her own family.
facts.quote: He was so cheerful—and so good at dancing the foxtrot.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)

facts.text: Brian was killed in a plane crash about three years later, flying to join her in London.
facts.quote: I wasn't overwhelmed with grief. I missed him but I remembered the good times and how bright he was.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)

facts.text: After a meal with British friends at a grand Shanghai hotel, she met a starving man at the gate asking for a few cents. She went home and threw out her lipstick, rouge and nail polish.
facts.quote: I'll never touch a cent that belongs to the poor person. That was the start. After that, I was free.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Khng Eu Meng, 'Teresa Hsu: Never too old to care for others', Singapore's Extraordinary People (1995), reprinted on cme4all wiki
Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)

facts.text: At 47, far past the age limit, she wrote to the Nursing Council in London; the matron replied that they were touched and would train her.
facts.quote: I'm grossly overaged, but for me, it's a dedication, not a livelihood.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Khng Eu Meng, 'Teresa Hsu: Never too old to care for others', Singapore's Extraordinary People (1995), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: She trained without fees at the Royal Free Hospital, London.

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
SeniorsAloud, 'Meet Angel of Compassion - Teresa Hsu' (Dec 2008; author met her 20 Oct 2008)

facts.text: She spent eight years in England, nursing in hospitals and travelling across Europe with the International Voluntary Service for Peace.

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
SeniorsAloud, 'Meet Angel of Compassion - Teresa Hsu' (Dec 2008; author met her 20 Oct 2008)

facts.text: She became a conscious vegetarian while watching fish play in a river (she said she had never digested meat since birth).
facts.quote: We humans have no right to end their fun.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: International Vegetarian Union, 'Interview with 110-year-old vegetarian' (c. 2008)
Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih

facts.text: She sailed to Paraguay with the Bruderhof (Society of Brothers) and stayed eight years, often the only trained nurse and midwife at a small hospital.

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)

facts.text: A letter from home called her back to her ageing mother in Penang.
facts.quote: Poor people you get everywhere, but you have only one mother.
facts.speaker: her mother, as Teresa recalled it (Her World, 1999)

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)

facts.text: In Malaysia she helped her brother Anthony, a Catholic priest, set up the Assunta Hospital for the poor and served as its matron.

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih

facts.text: She forgave her father; when he fell ill she brought him from China to Singapore and nursed him until he died.

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)

facts.text: In Singapore she became the unsalaried matron of Kwong Wai Shiu Hospital.

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
Singapore Women's Hall of Fame (SCWO), 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (inducted 2014)

facts.text: With elder sister Ursula, principal of CHIJ Bukit Timah, who paid for it, she opened the Home for the Aged Sick on a 0.6-hectare plot with a bungalow at Jalan Payoh Lai, one of Singapore's first homes for the elderly sick.
facts.quote: My sister supported me, she was the one who bought this land for me.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih
The Straits Times, Friday Interview and timeline (31 Dec 1999), reprinted on cme4all wiki
Singapore Women's Hall of Fame (SCWO), 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (inducted 2014)

facts.text: The sisters turned the bungalow and servants' quarters into wards. Ursula paid from her salary; Teresa ran the home and sold the fruit of 10 coconut trees and a dozen banana trees in the backyard.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih
NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)

facts.text: With about 100 patients and no money to cope, they handed the deeds to the Society for the Aged Sick, formed by Rotary Club members, which built three blocks; she stayed on as matron.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih
SeniorsAloud, 'Meet Angel of Compassion - Teresa Hsu' (Dec 2008; author met her 20 Oct 2008)
NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)

facts.text: Ursula died and left Teresa 'a small fortune'. She used it to buy flats for people with nowhere to go: five in Singapore, two in Malaysia.

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
Khng Eu Meng, 'Teresa Hsu: Never too old to care for others', Singapore's Extraordinary People (1995), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: Lucy and Anthony died within weeks of each other, leaving her without family.

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)

facts.text: The home's chief cook, Madam Anjelei, remembered being paid extra; her son Maran called Teresa his godmother, who made sure the family bought a flat.
facts.quote: She paid me more as I had many children.
facts.speaker: Madam Anjelei, former chief cook

sources.label: Khng Eu Meng, 'Teresa Hsu: Never too old to care for others', Singapore's Extraordinary People (1995), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: Lim Soon Kheam, former treasurer of the Society for the Aged Sick, said she gave up her own luxury bungalow and took no salary.
facts.quote: She's one of the rare kind who gave up her own property, a luxury bungalow, to house the aged sick.
facts.speaker: Lim Soon Kheam

sources.label: Khng Eu Meng, 'Teresa Hsu: Never too old to care for others', Singapore's Extraordinary People (1995), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: She took up yoga at 69 after buying a book called Forever Young, Forever Healthy, and later taught it at temples, hospitals and schools.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih
NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
SeniorsAloud, 'Meet Angel of Compassion - Teresa Hsu' (Dec 2008; author met her 20 Oct 2008)

facts.text: Her mother, Tan Sok Chan, died aged 104.

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)

facts.text: She retired as the home's matron (1980, 1983 or 1985, depending on the source) and moved into a small flat attached to it.

sources.label: NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)
Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih

facts.text: She renamed her informal charity Friends of the Poor as Heart to Heart Service. With co-worker Sharana Rao and volunteer drivers, she took rice, sugar, biscuits and S$20 to S$180 a month to elderly people on public assistance.

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih
NLB Infopedia, 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (valid as at 2016; read via Wayback copy of SIP_1590)

facts.text: She paid for the S$2,000-a-month dialysis of Ong Teck Khoon after his brother described his plight in a newspaper.
facts.quote: Then Nurse Hse came. I'm grateful to her. She's my saviour.
facts.speaker: Ong Teck Khoon

sources.label: Khng Eu Meng, 'Teresa Hsu: Never too old to care for others', Singapore's Extraordinary People (1995), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: Outside her flat, an orange plant someone had thrown away carried her handwritten tag with its 'date of rebirth'.
facts.quote: A live thing should never be left alone to die.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)

facts.text: Her flat held a 2,000-volume library she called Prema ('divine love'), a formica table held together with tape, and a Bhagavad Gita on its seventh reading.
facts.quote: Everything I am, I learnt from these books.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)
Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih
SeniorsAloud, 'Meet Angel of Compassion - Teresa Hsu' (Dec 2008; author met her 20 Oct 2008)

facts.text: She kept no pictures except yellowing photos of her mother and Ursula, and thanked them every morning and night.
facts.quote: I thank them every morning and night for inspiring me to be good.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Her World, 'Her World Special Award 1999: Teresa Hsu' (interview at her flat, 1999)

facts.text: Asked in a Straits Times interview whether Singapore's old and sick were well cared for, she said no and urged S$500 a month in public assistance.
facts.quote: No, no, no, not at all. They are grossly neglected.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: The Straits Times, Friday Interview and timeline (31 Dec 1999), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: A visitor found her barefoot in a spotless flat; she cleaned it herself and could not afford a 65-cent newspaper, having no income.
facts.quote: I know what you think. Who cleans the rooms? I clean it myself.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Mary Kogan, letter, The Straits Times Forum (5 Feb 2000), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: She ate sparely: water or milk for breakfast, milk and salad or blended juice for lunch, yoghurt for dinner.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Teresa Hsu Chih
Mary Kogan, letter, The Straits Times Forum (5 Feb 2000), reprinted on cme4all wiki

facts.text: She explained why she never married.
facts.quote: If I'm married, I make only one man happy. If I'm not married, I make many people happy.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: SeniorsAloud, 'Meet Angel of Compassion - Teresa Hsu' (Dec 2008; author met her 20 Oct 2008)

facts.text: At 110 she sang visitors a German song and a Cantonese nursery rhyme, and read the words 'Living is Giving' off a pen without glasses.
facts.quote: I hope to live till 250! In this world, there are still many poor people who need help from others.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: SeniorsAloud, 'Meet Angel of Compassion - Teresa Hsu' (Dec 2008; author met her 20 Oct 2008)

facts.text: She received the Public Service Star.

sources.label: Singapore Women's Hall of Fame (SCWO), 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (inducted 2014)
Heart to Heart Service, 'About Founder' and Sharana Rao's announcement (Wayback, 2012)

facts.text: At a Penang talk to about 200 people she was asked whether she had ever been ill.
facts.quote: The sick demons forgot to visit me.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: K. Kasturi Dewi, 'The Power of Laughter', The Star (26 Jan 2010), reprinted on tsemrinpoche.com

facts.text: In 2010 she explained sharing as multiplied joy: eating alone makes one person laugh, sharing with 20 makes 21 laugh.
facts.quote: If I eat food by myself, I alone 'haha chiou'. If I share with 20 people, 21 people 'haha chiou'.
facts.speaker: Teresa Hsu

sources.label: Singapore Women's Hall of Fame (SCWO), 'Teresa Hsu Chih' (inducted 2014)

facts.text: She died peacefully at home on Wednesday 7 December 2011, aged 113. By her instruction she was cremated the same day, with no rituals or announcement, and no one claimed her ashes.

sources.label: Heart to Heart Service, 'About Founder' and Sharana Rao's announcement (Wayback, 2012)
